abdominal-aortic-aneurysm: An abdominal aortic aneurysm occurs when a section of the aorta—the large blood vessel carrying blood from your heart through your abdomen—expands beyond its normal diameter.
abortion-in-germany: This article concerns care in Germany. Abortion access depends on the legal route, pregnancy duration and clinical circumstances.
acne: Acne involves blocked hair follicles and inflammation. It can produce blackheads, whiteheads, inflamed spots and deeper painful lumps, often on the face, chest or back.
acute-bronchitis: Acute bronchitis is temporary inflammation of the larger airways in the lungs, commonly during or after a viral respiratory infection. Coughing may continue after a sore throat or runny nose has improved.
acute-cystitis: Cystitis is inflammation of the bladder, commonly caused by a bacterial infection. Burning when passing urine, needing to urinate frequently and discomfort low in the abdomen are typical concerns.
acute-pancreatitis: Acute pancreatitis is sudden inflammation of the pancreas, an organ that helps digest food and produces hormones including insulin. It can become serious and needs urgent hospital assessment.
after-the-baby-is-born: The period after birth involves physical healing, learning to care for a newborn and adjusting to interrupted sleep. Recovery varies with the birth, complications and support available.
age-related-farsightedness-presbyopia: Presbyopia is a gradual reduction in the eye's ability to focus on nearby objects as its natural lens becomes less flexible with age. Reading small print or looking at a phone may become harder even when distance vision seems clear.
age-related-macular-degeneration-amd: Age-related macular degeneration, or AMD, affects the macula, the part of the retina used for sharp central vision. Reading, recognising faces and seeing detail can become difficult even when some side vision remains useful.
alcohol: Alcohol-related problems are not defined only by a single drink count. Difficulty controlling drinking, repeated harm and withdrawal symptoms can all matter.
allergic-contact-dermatitis: Allergic contact dermatitis is an itchy skin inflammation caused by an immune reaction to something touching the skin. It often develops after a delay, so the last product you used is not necessarily the cause.
allergies: An allergy happens when your immune system treats a harmless substance as a threat and launches a defense response. Common triggers include pollen, certain foods, insect stings, pet dander, and medications.
allergies-to-animals: An animal allergy is an immune reaction to proteins associated with an animal, including proteins in skin flakes, saliva or urine. Hair can carry these substances, but hair itself is not the whole explanation.
alzheimers-disease: Alzheimer’s disease is a progressive brain condition and a cause of dementia. Dementia describes difficulties with thinking that affect daily life, rather than ordinary occasional forgetfulness.
alzheimers-disease-understanding-the-res: A responder analysis counts how many study participants meet a defined outcome, rather than reporting only an average score. It can make research easier to discuss, but the word responder does not necessarily mean recovery or improvement.
alzheimers-disease-what-is-the-cdr-scale: The Clinical Dementia Rating, or CDR, is a structured assessment of how thinking and memory difficulties affect everyday life. A trained professional combines information from the person and someone who knows them well.
ankle-fractures: An ankle fracture is a break in a bone around the ankle joint. Some fractures are stable, while others affect alignment or joint stability and need more involved treatment.
ankle-sprains: An ankle sprain injures the ligaments that support the joint, often when the foot twists. Pain, swelling and bruising can follow, but these symptoms also occur with fractures and other injuries.
anticoagulants-how-can-you-prevent-bleed: Anticoagulants reduce the chance of harmful blood clots but also make bleeding easier or harder to stop. Safer use means taking the right medicine as prescribed, checking interactions and knowing when to seek help.
appendicitis: Appendicitis is inflammation of the appendix, a small structure attached to the bowel. It can worsen and cause serious complications, so suspected appendicitis needs urgent medical assessment.
asthma: Asthma causes variable inflammation and narrowing of the airways. Wheezing, cough, chest tightness and breathlessness may come and go, including at night or with activity.
at-the-doctors: A useful medical appointment brings together your experience and the clinician's assessment. You do not need to know the diagnosis before asking for help.
at-the-hospital: A hospital visit may be an outpatient appointment, a day procedure or an overnight stay. Knowing why you are attending and who is responsible for the next step can reduce uncertainty.
athletes-foot: Athlete’s foot is a fungal infection of the skin of the feet, not a condition limited to athletes. It can cause itching, scaling and cracks, often between the toes, but may also affect the soles or sides.
atrial-fibrillation: Atrial fibrillation, or AF, is an abnormal electrical rhythm in the heart's upper chambers that often produces an irregular pulse. It may come and go or remain present, and some people notice no symptoms.
atrial-flutter: Atrial flutter is a heart rhythm problem in which an electrical signal circulates repeatedly through the upper chambers, making them beat rapidly. The pulse you feel may be fast and regular or sometimes irregular.
attention-deficit-hyperactivity-disorder: Attention deficit hyperactivity disorder, or ADHD, affects attention, impulse control and activity regulation. It begins in childhood, although some people are recognised only as adults.
autism: Autism is a lifelong difference in development that can affect communication, social interaction, sensory experience and patterns of interests or activity. Autistic people vary greatly in abilities and support needs.
av-block-heart-block: Atrioventricular block, or AV block, means electrical signals from the upper heart chambers reach the lower chambers too slowly or not reliably. It is different from a blocked coronary artery, although heart disease can cause both.
babys-first-weeks-newborn-check-ups: Newborn check-ups combine physical examination, feeding support and screening for conditions that may not be visible at birth. An appointment is also a chance to discuss your concerns and arrange follow-up.
bacterial-vaginosis: Bacterial vaginosis, or BV, involves a change in the balance of bacteria in the vagina. It can cause an unusual discharge or smell, while some people have no symptoms.
bakers-cysts: A Baker's cyst is a pocket of joint fluid that forms behind the knee. It can feel like a soft lump and cause tightness, pain or difficulty bending the joint, although some cysts cause no trouble.
balanitis-inflammation-of-the-head-of-th: Balanitis means inflammation of the glans, the head of the penis. The foreskin may also be inflamed.
bedbugs: Bedbugs are insects that hide near sleeping places and feed on blood. Finding them can be upsetting, but an infestation does not mean a home is dirty.
bedwetting: Bedwetting during sleep is common in younger children and is not laziness or deliberate misbehaviour. Night-time bladder control develops at different rates.
before-surgery-getting-information-and-m: Being offered an operation does not mean every important question has already been answered. A planned procedure should have a clear purpose, a discussion of benefits and harms, and preparation suited to your health and circumstances.
benign-enlarged-prostate: Benign prostate enlargement is non-cancerous growth of the prostate, a gland below the bladder. Enlargement can affect urine flow, but not every urinary symptom comes from the prostate.
benign-paroxysmal-positional-vertigo: Benign paroxysmal positional vertigo, or BPPV, causes brief bursts of spinning with particular head movements. It is an inner-ear balance problem and can often be treated with repositioning movements.
biologics-and-biosimilars: Biological medicines are made using living systems. They include many different treatments, such as some medicines for inflammatory diseases, cancer and diabetes.
birth: Birth involves physical changes, decisions and support for both the person giving birth and the baby. Labour does not follow an identical timetable for everyone.
bladder-training: Bladder training is a behavioural approach to troublesome urgency, frequency and some urine leakage. It uses a planned toilet routine and ways of responding to urgency, adjusted gradually with professional advice.
blood-test-for-down-edwards-and-patau-sy: Non-invasive prenatal testing, or NIPT, is a blood test during pregnancy that estimates the chance of certain chromosome conditions. Common panels screen for Down, Edwards and Patau syndromes.
boils-and-carbuncles: A boil is a painful, pus-filled skin infection, often starting around a hair follicle. Several connected boils can form a larger infected area called a carbuncle.
brachytherapy: Brachytherapy places a sealed radiation source in or close to the area being treated. It can deliver radiation locally while limiting exposure to some nearby tissue, but healthy tissue can still be affected.
brain-aneurysm: A brain aneurysm is a bulge in an artery in or near the brain. Many are found incidentally and never rupture, but a rupture can cause life-threatening bleeding.
breast-cancer: Breast cancer starts when abnormal breast cells grow and may invade nearby tissue or spread elsewhere. It can affect people of different ages and genders.
breast-cancer-treating-lymphedema: Breast cancer treatment can disrupt lymph drainage, especially when lymph nodes or nearby tissue are affected by surgery or radiation. Fluid may then build up in an arm, hand, breast or chest area.
bruised-knee: A direct blow or fall can bruise the soft tissues around the knee, causing tenderness, swelling and skin colour changes. A bruise may be minor, but the same incident can also injure bone, cartilage or ligaments.
bunions: A bunion is a change in alignment around the big-toe joint, often with a bony prominence on the inner side of the foot. The big toe may lean towards the others, causing crowding, rubbing or pain.
bursitis: Bursae are small fluid-containing sacs that reduce friction between tissues near joints. When a bursa becomes inflamed, the area may be painful, tender or swollen.
calcium-calculator: Estimating calcium from food can help an adult understand their diet and discuss whether changes are useful. The result is approximate: portions, brands and day-to-day eating vary.
can-measurements-show-if-a-treatment-wor: Blood tests, scans and other measurements can help diagnose illness, monitor treatment and detect harm. But a better number does not automatically answer every question about benefit.
can-mothers-reduce-their-childs-risk-of-: Parents sometimes avoid milk, eggs, nuts or other foods hoping to prevent eczema in their baby. Routine exclusion of common food allergens during pregnancy or breastfeeding is not recommended solely for that purpose.
can-noise-damage-your-hearing: Loud sound can injure the delicate structures of the inner ear. Damage may follow a single intense sound, such as an explosion, or build up through repeated exposure at work, through music or during hobbies.
cancer-what-do-the-codes-in-the-doctors-: A cancer letter can contain several kinds of shorthand: where the cancer began, how far it extends, what its cells look like and what tests or treatment have already happened. These codes help professionals communicate.
canker-sores-mouth-ulcers: An aphthous ulcer, often called a canker sore, is a painful shallow sore in the lining of the mouth. It may make eating, brushing and talking uncomfortable even when it is small.
cardiopulmonary-resuscitation-cpr-what-y: If someone is unresponsive now, call emergency services immediately: 112 in the European Union and Moldova, or the local emergency number elsewhere. Put the phone on speaker and follow the dispatcher's instructions.
carpal-tunnel-syndrome: Carpal tunnel syndrome happens when the median nerve is compressed as it passes through a narrow space at the wrist. It can cause tingling, numbness, pain and difficulty using the hand.
cataract-surgery: Cataract surgery removes the cloudy natural lens and replaces it with an artificial lens inside the eye. For many people it improves sight and daily activities, but the expected benefit depends on the rest of the eye as well as the cataract.
cataracts: A cataract is clouding of the eye's natural lens. It usually develops gradually with age, making vision hazy, colours less vivid or bright lights more troublesome.
causes-and-signs-of-edema: Edema means swelling caused by fluid collecting in body tissues. Shoes or rings may feel tight, an arm or leg may feel heavy, or the skin may look stretched.
celiac-disease: Celiac disease, also spelled coeliac disease, is an autoimmune condition in which gluten triggers damage to the small intestine. It is different from wheat allergy and from symptoms attributed to gluten without celiac disease.
cervical-cancer: Cervical cancer begins in the cervix, the lower part of the uterus that opens into the vagina. Most cases are linked to persistent infection with certain high-risk human papillomaviruses, or HPV.
cervical-cancer-how-are-precancerous-cel: Abnormal cells on the cervix are often called dysplasia or cervical intraepithelial neoplasia, abbreviated CIN. These changes are not the same as invasive cervical cancer.
chickenpox: Chickenpox, or varicella, is a very contagious infection caused by the varicella-zoster virus. It often causes an itchy rash with spots, blisters and crusts present at the same time, together with fever or feeling unwell.
children-and-sun-practical-information-f: Outdoor play is valuable, and sun protection can be part of the plan before a child gets uncomfortable. Ultraviolet radiation can damage skin and eyes even when the weather does not feel very hot.
chlamydia: Chlamydia is a bacterial sexually transmitted infection that often causes no symptoms. A person can carry and pass it on without knowing, so feeling well does not rule it out.
chronic-kidney-disease: Chronic kidney disease, or CKD, means a lasting abnormality of kidney structure or function, generally present for more than three months. Early disease often has no symptoms and does not automatically lead to dialysis.
chronic-obstructive-pulmonary-disease-co: Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, or COPD, causes lasting airflow limitation from damage to the airways and lungs. It can involve chronic bronchitis, emphysema or both.
chronic-wounds: A chronic wound stays open, heals unusually slowly or repeatedly breaks down. Good dressings matter, but healing also depends on the cause: blood supply, pressure, swelling, nerve damage, infection and general health can all contribute.
climate-and-health: Climate change affects health through hotter conditions, extreme weather, air quality, food and water security and disruption of essential services. The risks differ by place and by a person's health, housing, work and access to help.
cluster-headache: Cluster headache is a disorder causing exceptionally severe attacks, usually around an eye or temple on one side.
cognitive-behavioral-therapy-cbt: Cognitive behavioural therapy, or CBT, is a family of structured psychological treatments that explore connections between thoughts, emotions, bodily reactions and actions. A trained therapist works with you on agreed problems and goals.
cold-sores: Cold sores are outbreaks of herpes simplex infection, usually causing painful blisters on or near the lips. Tingling, itching or burning may start before the blisters appear.
colorectal-cancer: Colorectal cancer begins in the colon or rectum, which are parts of the large bowel. Some cancers develop from polyps, although many polyps never become cancer.
comments-praise-and-criticism: Clear health information improves when readers can point out confusing wording, missing explanations and barriers to access. This is a health-literacy guide about giving useful feedback, not a medical-condition article.
common-colds: A runny nose, scratchy throat and cough often come from a viral infection of the upper airways. Most ordinary colds settle with time and simple care.
complications-of-gallstones: Gallstones can remain silent for years, but a stone that obstructs drainage can cause more than a painful attack. Inflammation of the gallbladder, infection of the bile ducts or inflammation of the pancreas may need urgent hospital treatment.
concussion: Concussion is a brain injury caused by a blow or sudden jolt to the head or body. You do not have to lose consciousness to have one.
conjunctivitis-pink-eye: Conjunctivitis is inflammation of the thin covering over the white of the eye and inside the eyelids. Infection, allergy and irritants can cause similar-looking redness.
corns: A corn is a small area of thickened skin, often with a dense centre that hurts when pressed. A callus is usually a broader patch of hard skin.
coronary-artery-disease: The heart muscle needs its own supply of oxygen-rich blood. Coronary artery disease develops when disease in the vessels supplying it restricts that supply, commonly because fatty plaques build up in the artery walls.
cough: Coughing helps clear the airways, but an irritating or persistent cough can disturb sleep, work and daily life. A cough is a symptom rather than a single disease.
covid-19-coronavirus-disease: COVID is an infection caused by SARS-CoV-2. It can resemble a cold, but it can also cause severe illness or lasting symptoms.
cpap-therapy-for-sleep-apnea-dealing-wit: CPAP uses air pressure through a mask to keep the upper airway open during sleep. It treats obstructive sleep apnoea while it is being used; it is not simply a machine to stop snoring.
croup: Croup is usually a viral illness that causes swelling around a young child's voice box and windpipe. The cough may sound like a bark, with a hoarse voice and sometimes a harsh noise on breathing in, called stridor.
crowns-bridges-implants-what-types-of-re: A damaged or missing tooth does not have one automatic solution. A crown can protect a remaining tooth, while a bridge, an implant-supported restoration or a removable denture may replace missing teeth.
decision-aids: Some health decisions have more than one reasonable option. A patient decision aid explains a specific choice, compares benefits and harms and helps you consider what matters to you.
deep-vein-thrombosis-dvt: Deep-vein thrombosis is a blood clot in a deep vein, usually in a leg but sometimes in an arm or the pelvis. It needs prompt assessment because a clot can grow or part can travel to the lungs, causing a pulmonary embolism.
dehydration: Dehydration happens when the body loses more fluid than it takes in. Vomiting, diarrhoea, fever, heavy sweating or difficulty getting drinks can all contribute.
depression: Depression can affect mood, interest, energy, sleep, thinking and physical health. It is a treatable illness, not a test of character or gratitude.
depression-after-childbirth-what-can-hel: Having a baby can bring joy alongside exhaustion, anxiety or sadness. Postnatal depression is more than a difficult day or a failure to be a good parent.
deviated-septum-in-the-nose-nasal-septal: The septum is the wall of cartilage and bone separating the nasal passages. It is rarely perfectly straight.
diabetic-foot-how-can-you-prevent-wounds: Diabetes can damage the nerves and blood supply in the feet. A blister may be painless yet become a serious wound, so pain is not a reliable guide to safety.
diarrhea: Diarrhoea means loose or watery stools more often than is normal for you. Sudden episodes often follow an infection and improve within days, but not every episode is a stomach bug.
dietary-advice-and-nutritional-therapy-s: Nutrition advice can help people build everyday eating habits, while nutrition therapy addresses the needs created by a medical condition. The useful starting point is your health, circumstances and goals, rather than a universal meal plan.
dietary-supplements-what-do-you-need-to-: Supplements include vitamins, minerals, herbs and other concentrated ingredients sold as tablets, drops, powders or drinks. Some have a clear role, such as treating a deficiency or meeting a specific life-stage need.
disease-management-program-for-type-1-di: A disease management programme, or DMP, organises continuing care for a chronic condition. In Germany, the diabetes programme brings planned reviews, education and coordination into an individual treatment plan.
dislocated-kneecap: A dislocated kneecap has slipped out of the groove at the front of the thighbone, usually toward the outside of the knee. A twist or impact can cause it, and some knee shapes make it more likely.
diverticular-disease-and-diverticulitis: Diverticula are small pouches in the wall of the large bowel. Many people have them without symptoms, called diverticulosis.
donanemab-kisunla-for-early-stage-alzhei: Donanemab is an antibody treatment that helps remove amyloid deposits from the brain. It may slow decline in some people with early symptomatic Alzheimer's disease, but it does not cure the disease or restore lost abilities.
down-edwards-and-patau-syndrome: These chromosome conditions affect development before birth and can create lifelong health and support needs. A test result is important information, but it does not describe a child's personality or predict every ability or medical problem.
drug-allergies: A drug allergy is an immune reaction to a medicine. It is different from many predictable side effects, but both can need medical attention.
drugs-assessed-by-iqwig: A new medicine can be authorised for use without being better than the treatment already available.
dust-mite-allergies: A dusty room can irritate anyone, but dust mite allergy is a specific immune reaction to proteins associated with tiny mites. These animals commonly live in mattresses and other soft furnishings.
eczema: Atopic eczema is an inflammatory condition that makes skin itchy, dry and easily irritated. It often starts in childhood but can persist or begin in adults.
eczema-can-eliminating-particular-foods-: It is understandable to look for a food that explains repeated eczema flares. Some people have both eczema and food allergy, but eczema does not mean that ordinary foods must be removed.
eczema-in-children-can-prebiotics-or-pro: Parents with a family history of eczema often ask whether a supplement could protect their baby.
endometriosis: Endometriosis involves tissue similar to the womb lining growing outside the womb. It can cause inflammation, scarring, pelvic pain and fertility difficulties, although symptoms vary widely.
enlarged-hemorrhoids: Haemorrhoidal cushions are normal blood-vessel and supporting tissues inside the anal canal. When enlarged or displaced, they can cause bleeding, itching, mucus or a bulge.
enlarged-tonsils-and-adenoids: Tonsils sit on either side of the throat; adenoids sit behind the nose. Both are immune tissues that can become large in childhood without being infected.
epidurals-and-other-medications-to-relie: Labour pain differs between people and can change as birth progresses. Wanting medicine is a valid choice, and changing your earlier plan is not a failure.
epilepsy: Epilepsy involves a lasting tendency to have epileptic seizures caused by abnormal electrical activity in the brain. Seizures do not always cause shaking: some briefly interrupt awareness or produce unusual sensations.
erysipelas-and-cellulitis: Erysipelas and cellulitis are bacterial infections of the skin and underlying tissues. They can start through a crack or wound too small to notice and often affect a leg, although other areas can be involved.
evaluating-the-evidence: A published study is not automatically a dependable answer to a treatment question. The way participants were selected, treatments compared and outcomes measured can change what a result means.
evidence-based-medicine-in-germany: Evidence-based medicine brings together reliable research, clinical expertise and the person’s circumstances and preferences. In Germany, it informs clinical recommendations and decisions within the health system.
evidence-the-cornerstone-of-our-informat: A useful health article should help you understand a decision, rather than persuade you to buy a product or accept a single treatment. Research provides a foundation, but choosing, explaining and updating that research also matters.
external-radiotherapy: External radiotherapy uses a machine outside the body to deliver radiation to a planned treatment area. It may aim to cure cancer, reduce the chance of recurrence or relieve symptoms.
eye-health-who-can-you-go-to: Eye care involves several professions whose qualifications and permitted activities differ between countries. A routine glasses appointment, an examination for eye disease and urgent assessment are not interchangeable.
falls-in-older-people: A fall is not an unavoidable part of growing older, and it should not be dismissed as clumsiness. Vision, balance, muscle strength, medicines, illness and the home environment can contribute together.
farsightedness-hyperopia: Hyperopia is a focusing problem in which light would come to a focus behind the retina when the eye is not compensating. Nearby tasks can be blurred or tiring, and higher degrees may affect distance vision too.
fast-heart-rate-in-paroxysmal-supraventr: Paroxysmal supraventricular tachycardia, or PSVT, causes episodes of a fast rhythm arising above the heart’s lower chambers. Episodes often start and stop abruptly and can feel frightening.
fasting: Medical fasting means avoiding specified food or drink for a defined period before a test, treatment or medicine. It is not the same as choosing a diet.
fever-in-children: A temperature of 38°C or more is generally considered a fever in children. Fever is a response to illness, often an infection, rather than a diagnosis itself.
fibromyalgia: Fibromyalgia is a long-term condition involving widespread pain, often with unrefreshing sleep, fatigue and difficulty concentrating. Symptoms are real even when routine tests do not show tissue damage.
finding-high-quality-health-information-: Searching online can help you prepare questions, but it can also expose you to advertising, misleading claims and advice that does not fit your situation. Start with a clear question and keep the source and its limitations visible.
first-aid-for-head-injuries: A blow to the head can affect the brain even without an obvious wound or loss of consciousness. Concussion may cause headache, dizziness, memory problems or difficulty concentrating.
food-allergies: Food allergy is an immune reaction to a food protein, and small amounts can sometimes cause serious illness. It differs from food intolerance and does not explain every symptom after eating.
foot-deformities: Feet vary naturally in arch height, toe alignment and flexibility. Flat arches, high arches, bunions and curled toes are different findings, not one diagnosis.
frozen-shoulder: Frozen shoulder, also called adhesive capsulitis, causes gradually increasing pain and restricted movement. Sleep, dressing and reaching can become difficult.
functional-dyspepsia: Functional dyspepsia can cause early fullness, burning or pain above the navel without an ulcer explaining the symptoms. The discomfort is real even when routine investigations are normal.
gallstones: Gallstones are solid deposits in the gallbladder or bile ducts. Many cause no symptoms, while an obstructing stone can cause intense upper abdominal pain and sometimes infection or pancreatitis.
gastritis: Gastritis means inflammation of the stomach lining. It may follow Helicobacter pylori infection, certain pain medicines or other causes; upper abdominal pain alone cannot confirm the diagnosis.
gathering-information-and-making-a-decis: A health decision may involve a test, treatment, procedure or continued observation. Reliable information helps, but the best choice also depends on your circumstances and priorities.
generalized-anxiety-disorder: Generalized anxiety disorder involves difficult-to-control worry across many parts of life. Muscle tension, poor sleep, restlessness and concentration problems can accompany it; it is more than ordinary occasional concern.
genital-herpes: Genital herpes is caused by herpes simplex viruses. Painful blisters or ulcers may recur, but many infections are unnoticed.
genital-warts: Genital warts are caused mainly by low-risk human papillomavirus types. These differ from the types responsible for most cancers, but different types may coexist and appropriate cervical screening remains important.
gestational-diabetes: Gestational diabetes is raised blood glucose first diagnosed during pregnancy. Often there are no symptoms.
gingivitis-and-periodontitis: Gingivitis is inflammation of the gums, commonly caused by plaque. Periodontitis affects deeper tooth-supporting tissues and bone.
giving-mouth-to-mouth-resuscitation: This guide concerns an adult who is unresponsive and not breathing normally. Call 112 immediately for an unresponsive person, use speakerphone and follow the dispatcher.
glaucoma: Glaucoma damages the optic nerve and can reduce the visual field. The common open-angle form often develops silently.
gluten-and-wheat-sensitivity-allergy-or-: Symptoms after wheat do not all have the same cause. Celiac disease is an immune reaction to gluten that damages the small bowel; wheat allergy and non-celiac sensitivity need different investigations and care.
going-to-see-a-gynecologist: Gynecology care can address bleeding, pelvic pain, contraception, pregnancy concerns or screening. A first visit does not automatically require an internal examination.
gonorrhea-the-clap: Gonorrhea is a bacterial sexually transmitted infection that may affect the genitals, rectum, throat or eyes. Many infections produce no symptoms; untreated infection can cause serious complications and can be passed on unknowingly.
gout: Gout is inflammation caused by urate crystals in joints. Attacks can be extremely painful, often affecting a big toe, ankle or knee.
graves-disease: Graves’ disease is an autoimmune condition that can make the thyroid produce excess hormone. It may cause palpitations, heat intolerance, tremor and weight loss; eye problems can occur independently of the degree of thyroid overactivity.
growing-body-of-knowledge-the-starting-p: Medical knowledge changes as researchers test questions, compare treatments and examine harms. Reliable health information explains both what is known and what remains uncertain.
growth-in-childhood-and-puberty: Children grow at different rates and puberty begins at different times. Height, weight and body proportions change through development.
hair-loss-in-chemotherapy: Some chemotherapy damages rapidly dividing hair-producing cells. Hair loss varies by medicine and dose and may involve the scalp, eyebrows, lashes and body.
hand-foot-and-mouth-disease: Hand, foot and mouth disease is a contagious viral illness, most common in young children but also possible in adults. Mouth sores and a hand or foot rash can occur; it is not the same as animal foot-and-mouth disease.
harvesting-blood-stem-cells-for-transpla: Blood-forming stem cells can be collected from circulating blood or bone marrow for transplantation. Collection is separate from the recipient’s conditioning and transplant treatment.
hashimotos-disease: Hashimoto’s disease is autoimmune inflammation of the thyroid. Over time it may reduce hormone production, but antibodies alone do not mean everyone needs immediate treatment.
hay-fever: Hay fever is an allergic response to pollen. Sneezing, an itchy or blocked nose and watery itchy eyes often follow a seasonal pattern.
head-lice: Head lice are small insects living on scalp hair. They spread mainly through head-to-head contact and are not a sign of poor cleanliness.
headaches: Headache is a symptom with many causes. Tension-type headache and migraine are common primary headache disorders; infection, injury or other illness can cause secondary headache.
health-care-in-germany: This article concerns services in Germany, not the rules in Moldova or every European country. Knowing where to ask for routine, urgent and emergency care can reduce delays and unnecessary journeys.
health-insurance-in-germany: People living in Germany generally need health insurance. Statutory and private systems have different eligibility, contributions and reimbursement arrangements.
hearing-loss-and-deafness-in-adults: Hearing loss can make conversation, work and warning sounds harder to follow. It may develop gradually or suddenly and affect one or both ears.
hearing-loss-and-deafness-in-children: Childhood hearing loss may be temporary or permanent, present from birth or develop later. Early assessment and access to an understandable language support learning and relationships.
hearing-tests-in-newborns: Newborn hearing screening looks for hearing differences before they are obvious. It is quick and does not diagnose every kind of hearing loss.
heart-failure: Heart failure means the heart cannot fill or pump effectively enough for the body’s needs. It is not the same as the heart stopping.
heart-rhythm-disorders-arrhythmias: Arrhythmias are heartbeats that are unusually fast, slow or irregular. Some extra beats are harmless, while other rhythms need urgent treatment.
heart-valve-diseases: Heart valves keep blood moving in the right direction. A narrowed valve obstructs flow, while a leaking valve allows backward flow.
heartburn-and-gerd: Reflux is stomach contents moving into the food pipe. Occasional heartburn is common; troublesome repeated symptoms or complications may indicate gastroesophageal reflux disease.
heavy-periods: Menstrual bleeding is heavy when its amount or duration disrupts life, not only when it meets a measured volume. It may cause iron deficiency and fatigue.
hemangioma: An infantile hemangioma is a benign growth of blood vessels, often appearing after birth and growing before gradually shrinking. Many need observation only, but location and growth can matter more than apparent size.
hemodialysis-for-chronic-kidney-disease: Hemodialysis removes waste and excess fluid from blood when kidneys cannot do enough. It supports life but does not replace every kidney function.
hemophilia: Hemophilia is a disorder of clotting proteins that can cause prolonged or internal bleeding. Inherited forms are more common in males, but females can also have significant bleeding.
hepatitis-b: Hepatitis B is a viral liver infection. Some infections clear, while others persist and need monitoring or treatment.
hepatitis-c: Hepatitis C is a blood-borne viral liver infection that may remain unnoticed for years. Effective tablet treatment can cure most infections, but cure does not automatically reverse established cirrhosis or protect against reinfection.
hernias: An abdominal hernia occurs when tissue pushes through a weakness in the abdominal wall. A groin, navel or previous surgical scar may bulge.
high-blood-pressure: High blood pressure often causes no symptoms but increases the risk of stroke, heart disease and kidney damage. Diagnosis and targets depend on repeated measurements and individual circumstances, not whether you feel tense or have a headache.
high-cholesterol: Cholesterol travels in blood particles and has normal body functions. Persistently high LDL cholesterol can contribute to artery disease.
hormone-therapy-for-menopause: Menopause hormone therapy can relieve troublesome hot flushes, night sweats and some related symptoms. It is an option, not an obligation.
how-are-genes-passed-on: Genes are sections of DNA that help cells make and regulate biological products. Inheritance passes genetic information from parents to children, but genes do not determine every trait or guarantee a disease.
how-are-hearing-and-speaking-connected: Hearing helps many people learn and monitor spoken language, but language is more than speech. Sign languages are complete languages, and deaf children can develop rich communication when given early accessible language and support.
how-are-our-muscles-structured-and-how-d: Muscles help us move, maintain posture, breathe and produce heat. Other muscle types pump blood and move material through internal organs.
how-are-sex-cells-made-meiosis: Meiosis is a special form of cell division involved in producing eggs and sperm. It reduces the chromosome set so fertilization can combine information from both biological parents.
how-can-gallstones-be-treated: Treatment depends on whether stones cause symptoms, where they are and whether complications are present. Removing the gallbladder is different from clearing a bile duct.
how-can-hearing-loss-be-prevented: Not all hearing loss can be prevented, and hearing differences are not a personal failure. Noise exposure, some infections, injuries and certain medicines are modifiable risks.
how-can-i-find-support-groups-and-inform: Illness can bring practical, emotional and administrative problems beyond the diagnosis itself. Peer groups and independent advice services can help in Germany, but their roles differ from clinical treatment.
how-can-informedhealthorg-help: InformedHealth is the English-language health information service of Germany’s IQWiG. It explains evidence about conditions, tests and treatments.
how-can-labor-be-induced: Labor induction starts or prepares labor before it begins spontaneously. It may be offered when continuing pregnancy carries more risk, but the reason, timing and options are individual.
how-can-you-get-enough-calcium: Calcium supports bones and teeth, muscle contraction and nerve signaling. Needs vary with age and circumstances.
how-can-you-get-enough-iron: Iron helps blood carry oxygen and supports other body functions. Needs vary with growth, pregnancy, menstruation and diet.
how-can-you-monitor-and-adjust-treatment: Vitamin K antagonists such as warfarin reduce clotting and help prevent dangerous clots. Too little effect may leave clot risk; too much increases bleeding.
how-do-bowel-movements-work: Bowel movements empty stool through a coordinated process involving the colon, rectum, nerves and pelvic-floor muscles. Normal frequency differs between people.
how-do-cancer-cells-grow-and-spread: Cancer develops when changes in cells allow abnormal growth and survival. It is not one disease: behavior differs greatly between types.
how-do-common-types-of-headaches-differ: Headache types overlap, and location or severity alone cannot establish a diagnosis. Tension-type headache and migraine are common; cluster headache is less common but very disabling.
how-do-dermatomes-help-in-the-diagnosis-: A dermatome is an area of skin mainly linked to a spinal nerve root. Patterns of pain, tingling or reduced sensation can help localize a problem, but a diagram is a guide rather than a diagnosis.
how-do-hands-work: Hands combine movement, touch and strength for tasks from fastening a button to lifting a bag.
how-do-implantable-cardioverter-defibril: An implantable cardioverter-defibrillator, or ICD, watches for certain dangerous heart rhythms and can treat them automatically.
how-do-joints-work: Joints connect bones and guide movement while sharing load. Their structure varies with their task: a shoulder allows broad motion, while a knee combines bending with controlled rotation.
how-do-lungs-work: The lungs move oxygen from inhaled air into blood and remove carbon dioxide. Breathing depends on airways, tiny air sacs, circulation and breathing muscles together.
how-do-most-cells-divide-mitosis: Cell division supports growth, tissue renewal and repair. Mitosis divides the copied genetic material into new nuclei, usually followed by separation into daughter cells.
how-do-teeth-and-the-periodontium-work: Teeth cut and grind food and contribute to speech and appearance. They are held by a living support system called the periodontium.
how-do-the-bones-work: Bones support movement, protect organs and store minerals. Marrow inside some bones produces blood cells.
how-do-the-female-sex-organs-work: Understanding reproductive anatomy can help describe symptoms, discuss sexual health and make informed choices. Bodies vary naturally, and a person’s organs do not determine their worth or identity.
how-do-the-kidneys-work: The kidneys filter blood, adjust water and salts and help maintain acid balance. They also support blood-pressure control, red-cell production and bone health.
how-do-the-parathyroid-glands-work: The parathyroid glands are small glands usually behind the thyroid. They make parathyroid hormone, which helps control calcium in blood.
how-do-the-tonsils-work: Tonsils are part of the immune system near the entrance to the airways and digestive tract. They help recognize germs, particularly during childhood, but do not form a perfect barrier.
how-do-ultrasound-examinations-work: Ultrasound uses high-frequency sound waves and their returning echoes to form images inside the body. It does not use ionizing radiation.
how-do-you-use-an-automated-external-def: An automated external defibrillator, or AED, analyzes heart rhythm and gives a shock only when indicated. Anyone can follow its prompts.
how-does-chemotherapy-work: Chemotherapy uses medicines that interfere with cancer-cell growth or survival. It is different from radiotherapy and from many targeted or immune treatments.
how-does-dialysis-work: Dialysis removes some waste products and excess water when kidneys cannot do enough. It supports balance rather than washing all substances out of blood.
how-does-mechanical-ventilation-work-dur: General anesthesia can reduce breathing and protective airway reflexes. The anesthesia team may support breathing while continuously monitoring the patient; the device chosen depends on the operation and individual risks.
how-does-our-sense-of-balance-work: Balance comes from cooperation between the inner ears, eyes, body-position sensors and brain. Dizziness is a symptom with many possible causes; understanding the system does not establish an ear diagnosis.
how-does-our-sense-of-taste-work: Flavor combines taste with smell, temperature and texture. A blocked nose can make meals seem bland even when tongue receptors work.
how-does-skin-work: Skin protects the body, limits water loss, senses contact and helps control temperature. Its layers have different jobs.
how-does-the-ankle-work: The ankle links the lower leg with the foot, carrying weight while adapting to the ground. Its joints, ligaments, tendons and muscles work together; pain after a twist is not automatically a minor sprain.
how-does-the-brain-work: The brain combines sensations, movement, memory and emotion while regulating vital functions. Different regions specialize but work in networks; a simple picture cannot predict someone's abilities, personality or recovery.
how-does-the-ear-work: Hearing involves the outer, middle and inner ear together with nerves and the brain. The inner ear also contains balance organs.
how-does-the-eye-work: Vision requires clear optical surfaces, a working retina, optic nerves and brain processing. Different structures do different jobs; poor sight is not always solved by stronger glasses, and a normal surface appearance cannot exclude disease.
how-does-the-gallbladder-work: The gallbladder stores and concentrates bile made by the liver. It helps deliver bile when needed for digestion but is not the organ that makes it.
how-does-the-heart-work: The heart is a muscular pump linking the lungs and the rest of the body. Its chambers, valves, electrical system and own blood supply cooperate.
how-does-the-immune-system-work: The immune system is a network of barriers, cells, organs and proteins, not a single strength setting. It must respond to threats while limiting injury to the body.
how-does-the-intestine-work: The intestine continues digestion after the stomach, absorbs nutrients and water, and moves waste toward the anus. Its lining, muscles, nerves and microbes cooperate.
how-does-the-knee-work: The knee links thigh and lower leg while allowing bending, straightening and limited rotation. Its stability depends on bones, ligaments and muscle control together.
how-does-the-larynx-work: The larynx sits between the throat and windpipe. It lets air pass, produces voice and helps keep food out of the airway.
how-does-the-liver-work: The liver processes nutrients, makes important proteins and bile, and changes many medicines and waste substances. It is not a filter that can be reset by a cleansing drink.
how-does-the-menstrual-cycle-work: The menstrual cycle links hormone signals, ovarian activity and changes in the uterine lining. Timing varies between people and across life.
how-does-the-nervous-system-work: The nervous system receives information, processes it and coordinates responses. It includes conscious movement and automatic regulation.
how-does-the-pancreas-work: The pancreas lies behind the stomach and has digestive and hormonal functions. These use different routes out of the organ.
how-does-the-pituitary-gland-work: The pituitary is a small gland beneath the brain linked to the hypothalamus. It helps coordinate other glands and several direct body functions.
how-does-the-prostate-work: The prostate is a gland below the bladder, surrounding part of the urethra. It contributes fluid to semen rather than producing sperm cells.
how-does-the-shoulder-work: The shoulder allows a wide range of movement while connecting the arm to the trunk. Several joints and the shoulder blade must cooperate.
how-does-the-spine-work: The spine is a chain of bones, joints and discs supported by muscles and ligaments. It carries load while protecting the spinal cord and nerve roots.
how-does-the-stomach-work: The stomach receives food from the esophagus, mixes it and releases small amounts into the intestine. It begins some digestion but does not absorb all nutrients.
how-does-the-thyroid-gland-work: The thyroid lies at the front of the neck and releases hormones that influence energy use, temperature and many body functions. Symptoms of imbalance overlap with other illnesses; weight or tiredness alone is not a thyroid diagnosis.
how-does-the-tongue-work: The tongue is a flexible muscular organ with a sensitive surface. It moves food, helps swallowing and shapes speech while detecting taste and touch.
how-does-the-urinary-system-work: The urinary system filters waste and excess water from your blood and removes them as urine. It includes the kidneys, the ureters, the bladder and the urethra.
how-does-ventilation-therapy-for-respira: Ventilation therapy uses a machine to help a person breathe when the lungs or breathing muscles cannot do the job well enough on their own.
how-is-blood-pressure-measured: Blood pressure is the force of blood pushing against the walls of your arteries.
how-is-body-temperature-regulated-and-wh: The human body keeps its core temperature within a narrow range, usually around 37 degrees Celsius, so that its cells and enzymes work well. Fever is a temporary rise in this set point, most often because the immune system is fighting an infection.
how-is-cervical-cancer-treated: Cervical cancer develops in the lower part of the womb, the cervix, usually after long-lasting infection with certain types of human papillomavirus. Abnormal cells often appear years before cancer forms and can be found by screening.
how-is-diabetes-diagnosed: Diabetes is diagnosed with blood tests that measure how much sugar, or glucose, is in the blood. Because early diabetes may cause no symptoms, testing is important for people at higher risk.
how-is-our-sleep-regulated: Sleep is controlled by two main systems: the body clock, which tells you when it is time to be awake or asleep, and the build-up of sleep pressure the longer you stay awake.
how-is-the-heart-rhythm-regulated: The heart beats because of its own electrical system, which starts each beat and coordinates the chambers so that they contract in the right order. The brain and hormones adjust the rate to your needs.
how-is-the-quality-of-studies-assessed: Not all studies are equally trustworthy. Some are designed and carried out in ways that make their results more reliable, while others carry a high risk of misleading conclusions.
how-much-sun-is-too-much: Sunlight supports mood and the production of vitamin D, but too much ultraviolet radiation damages skin cells and raises the risk of sunburn, premature skin ageing and skin cancer.
how-much-vitamin-d-do-we-need-and-how-ca: Vitamin D helps the body absorb calcium and keeps bones and muscles healthy. Most people make much of their vitamin D in the skin with the help of sunlight, and a smaller part comes from food.
how-our-content-is-structured: Health information comes in many forms, such as overviews, detailed articles, explanations of tests and treatments, and personal experiences.
how-our-teeth-and-jaws-work-together: Teeth and jaws form a precise system for biting, chewing, speaking and smiling. The upper and lower teeth meet in a pattern called the bite, and the jaw joints and chewing muscles move the lower jaw.
how-to-cut-toenails-properly: Cutting toenails the right way helps prevent painful ingrown nails, infections and pressure problems. A few simple habits, such as cutting straight across and not too short, protect your feet.
how-to-put-someone-into-the-recovery-pos: The recovery position keeps the airway open for a person who is unconscious but breathing normally. It lets fluid drain from the mouth and stops the tongue from blocking the throat.
hpv-vaccine-what-does-it-protect-against: The human papillomavirus vaccine protects against infection with the types of HPV that most often cause cervical cancer and several other cancers, as well as genital warts.
human-papillomaviruses-hpv-how-can-you-b: Human papillomaviruses are a large group of viruses that infect skin and mucous membranes. Most people are infected at some point in their lives without noticing.
hyperglycemia-and-hypoglycemia-in-type-2: People with type 2 diabetes may experience blood sugar that is too high, called hyperglycaemia, or too low, called hypoglycaemia. Recognising the signs and knowing what to do helps you stay safe and prevents emergencies.
hyperparathyroidism: The parathyroid glands are four tiny glands in the neck that control calcium levels in the blood. In hyperparathyroidism, one or more of them make too much parathyroid hormone, which raises blood calcium and can weaken the bones.
hysterectomy-surgical-removal-of-the-wom: A hysterectomy is an operation that removes the womb, sometimes together with the cervix, ovaries or fallopian tubes. It is performed for conditions such as fibroids, heavy bleeding, prolapse, endometriosis or cancer.
impaired-vision-what-can-help-in-everyda: Reduced vision or blindness can make everyday tasks harder, but many aids, techniques and services can help people stay independent. Support ranges from better lighting and magnifiers to mobility training and technology.
impetigo: Impetigo is a common, contagious bacterial skin infection, especially in young children. It causes red sores that burst and form honey-coloured crusts, often around the nose and mouth.
inducing-labor-when-your-baby-is-overdue: Most babies are born within a couple of weeks of their due date, but some pregnancies go beyond it.
infertility: Infertility means not becoming pregnant after a year of regular unprotected intercourse. It affects many couples and may be caused by factors in the woman, the man or both, and sometimes no cause is found.
influenza-the-flu: Influenza is a contagious viral infection of the nose, throat and lungs that occurs mostly in winter.
ingrown-toenail: An ingrown toenail occurs when the edge of a nail grows into the surrounding skin, causing pain, redness and sometimes infection. It most often affects the big toe.
insect-venom-allergies: Most insect stings cause only brief pain and swelling. In some people, the immune system overreacts to the venom of bees, wasps or hornets and causes a dangerous allergic reaction.
iron-deficiency-and-anemia: Iron is needed to make haemoglobin, the protein in red blood cells that carries oxygen. When the body lacks iron, tiredness and other symptoms develop, and anaemia may follow.
irritable-bowel-syndrome: Irritable bowel syndrome is a common long-term disorder of the gut that causes abdominal pain with diarrhoea, constipation or both. It does not damage the bowel or raise the risk of cancer, but symptoms can be distressing.
is-telemonitoring-a-good-idea-for-advanc: Telemonitoring means measuring things like weight, blood pressure, pulse or symptoms at home and sending them electronically to a healthcare team. In advanced heart failure, the aim is to notice worsening early and avoid hospital stays.
keeping-our-information-up-to-date: Medical knowledge changes as new studies appear, so reliable health information must be checked and revised regularly.
kidney-stones: Kidney stones are hard deposits made of minerals and salts that form in the kidneys and may travel down the urinary tract. Small stones often pass unnoticed, while larger ones can cause severe pain.
lactose-intolerance: Lactose intolerance means the body cannot digest milk sugar properly, causing bloating, wind and diarrhoea after dairy products. It is common in adults worldwide and is not dangerous.
lasting-pain-after-shingles: Some people continue to have burning or stabbing pain in the skin area where shingles occurred, long after the rash has healed. This is called postherpetic neuralgia.
lazy-eye-amblyopia-in-children: Amblyopia, often called lazy eye, is reduced vision in one eye because the brain does not learn to use it properly during childhood. The eye itself may look normal.
learning-disorders: Specific learning disorders are lasting difficulties in learning to read, spell or do arithmetic that cannot be explained by low intelligence or poor teaching. Dyslexia affects reading and spelling, and dyscalculia affects numbers and calculation.
lecanemab-leqembi-for-early-stage-alzhei: Lecanemab is an antibody medicine given by infusion that targets amyloid, a protein that builds up in the brain in Alzheimer's disease. It is intended for people in the early stages and may modestly slow the decline in memory and thinking.
light-therapy-tablets-and-injections: When creams and skin care are not enough to control atopic eczema, doctors may consider treatments that work on the whole body or use special light.
localized-prostate-cancer: Prostate cancer is one of the most common cancers in men. In many cases it is found while still confined to the prostate and grows slowly.
low-back-pain: Low back pain is very common and usually improves within weeks, even without a specific diagnosis. Staying active, using simple pain relief and avoiding prolonged bed rest are the cornerstones of recovery.
lyme-disease: Lyme disease is a bacterial infection transmitted through tick bites. It is common in forests and grassland in Europe and North America.
managing-pain-during-childbirth: Labour contractions are painful for most women, but pain varies widely between individuals. There are many ways to cope, from relaxation and movement to medicines and epidural anaesthesia.
mecfs-myalgic-encephalomyelitischronic-f: Myalgic encephalomyelitis or chronic fatigue syndrome, usually shortened to ME/CFS, is a serious long-term illness with severe exhaustion that does not improve with rest and gets worse after even minor physical or mental effort.
medically-unexplained-physical-symptoms: Many people have real physical symptoms, such as pain, dizziness, fatigue or palpitations, for which doctors find no clear physical disease. These are also called functional symptoms.
medication-list: A medication list records every medicine you take, including prescription drugs, over-the-counter products, vitamins and herbal remedies. Keeping it up to date helps doctors, pharmacists and carers avoid dangerous interactions and mistakes.
melanoma: Melanoma is a type of skin cancer that develops from pigment-producing cells. It is less common than other skin cancers but more dangerous because it can spread.
menopause: Menopause is the time when menstrual periods stop permanently, usually around the age of fifty. The years leading up to it, called perimenopause, bring hormonal changes that may cause hot flushes, sleep problems and mood changes.
mental-health-problems-where-can-you-fin: In Germany there are many places to turn to for help with mental health problems, from your family doctor to psychotherapists, outpatient clinics, counselling centres and telephone helplines.
metastatic-breast-cancer: Metastatic breast cancer means that cancer that began in the breast has spread to other parts of the body, such as bones, liver, lungs or brain.
middle-ear-infection: Middle ear infection, or otitis media, occurs when the space behind the eardrum becomes inflamed, usually after a cold. It is very common in young children and causes earache and sometimes fever.
migraine: Migraine is a common neurological condition that causes recurring attacks of moderate to severe headache, often with nausea and sensitivity to light and sound. Attacks last hours to days.
misaligned-teeth-and-jaws: Teeth that are crowded, crooked or do not meet properly may affect appearance, cleaning and sometimes chewing. Orthodontic treatment with braces or other appliances can move teeth and, in some cases, correct the jaw relationship.
moles-birthmarks-and-other-types-of-nevu: A nevus is a harmless collection of skin cells that appears as a mole or birthmark. Most people have between ten and fifty moles, and most are harmless.
motor-development-disorders: Children learn to sit, crawl, walk, grasp and run at different rates, but some have clear delays or difficulties with movement and coordination. Motor development disorders can affect play, school and self-esteem.
mouth-sores-what-can-you-do-yourself: Mouth sores such as canker sores and cold sores are very common and usually heal within a week or two without treatment. They can be painful, but simple measures reduce discomfort and speed healing.
mumps: Mumps is a contagious viral illness that classically causes painful swelling of the salivary glands in front of the ears. It spreads through coughing, sneezing and contact.
muscle-strains: A muscle strain is a stretch or small tear in a muscle or the tendon attached to it, usually from sudden overload during sport or lifting. It causes pain, tenderness and sometimes bruising.
nail-fungus: Nail fungus is a common infection that makes nails thick, discoloured and brittle. It affects toenails more often than fingernails and is not dangerous for most people, but it can be unsightly and sometimes uncomfortable.
neck-pain: Neck pain is common and usually caused by muscle strain or stiffness from posture, sleeping position or sudden movement. It generally improves within a few weeks.
negative-pressure-wound-therapy: Negative pressure wound therapy seals a special dressing over a wound and connects it to a pump that gently removes fluid by suction. It is used for wounds that heal slowly, such as pressure sores, diabetic foot ulcers and some surgical wounds.
non-melanoma-skin-cancer: Basal cell carcinoma and squamous cell carcinoma are the most common cancers worldwide. They usually develop on sun-exposed skin and grow slowly.
nosebleeds: Nosebleeds are common and usually harmless, caused by small blood vessels near the front of the nose breaking. They look alarming but can almost always be stopped at home within minutes.
obesity: Obesity means having a high amount of body fat that raises the risk of problems such as type 2 diabetes, high blood pressure, heart disease and joint problems.
obsessive-compulsive-disorder-ocd: Obsessive-compulsive disorder involves unwanted, distressing thoughts, images or urges called obsessions, and repetitive behaviours or mental acts called compulsions performed to reduce the distress. It is far more than being tidy or particular.
obstructive-sleep-apnea: In obstructive sleep apnoea, the airway repeatedly narrows or closes during sleep, causing pauses in breathing, loud snoring and fragmented sleep. It leads to daytime tiredness and raises the risk of high blood pressure, heart disease and accidents.
off-label-use-what-to-be-aware-of: Off-label use means using a medicine for a condition, age group, dose or route that is not covered by its official approval. It is common, especially for children, rare diseases and cancer, and can be reasonable when evidence supports it.
oral-thrush: Oral thrush is a fungal infection of the mouth caused by Candida yeast. It produces creamy white patches on the tongue and cheeks, soreness and a cottony feeling.
osteoarthritis: Osteoarthritis is the most common joint condition. It involves wear and changes in the cartilage and surrounding tissues, causing pain, stiffness and reduced movement, most often in knees, hips, hands and spine.
osteoarthritis-of-the-knee: Knee osteoarthritis is a long-term condition in which the cartilage and other tissues of the knee change over time, causing pain, stiffness and reduced movement. It is very common with increasing age.
osteoporosis-and-bone-fractures: Osteoporosis is a condition in which bones lose density and strength so that they break more easily, often after a minor fall. It develops silently over years and is more common in women after menopause and in older people.
outer-ear-infection: Outer ear infection, or otitis externa, is inflammation of the skin of the ear canal, often called swimmer's ear. It causes pain, itching and sometimes discharge.
ovarian-cysts: Ovarian cysts are fluid-filled sacs on or inside the ovary. Most are harmless, form as part of the normal menstrual cycle and disappear without treatment.
overactive-thyroid-hyperthyroidism: In hyperthyroidism, the thyroid gland produces too much thyroid hormone, speeding up the body's metabolism. It causes symptoms such as weight loss, a racing heart, nervousness and heat intolerance.
pain-after-surgery: Some pain after an operation is normal, but it can usually be controlled well. Good pain relief helps you breathe deeply, move early, sleep and recover faster.
pain-under-the-foot-plantar-fasciitis: Plantar fasciitis is one of the most common causes of heel pain. It affects the thick band of tissue running under the foot from the heel to the toes.
parkinsons-disease: Parkinson's disease is a progressive condition affecting movement, caused by the loss of nerve cells that produce dopamine in the brain. It leads to slowness, stiffness and tremor, and also non-motor symptoms.
passive-therapeutic-services: Passive therapies are treatments that are done to you rather than requiring your own active effort, such as massage, heat or cold packs, ultrasound, electrotherapy and manual therapy.
patellofemoral-pain-syndrome-runners-kne: Patellofemoral pain syndrome causes pain around or behind the kneecap, especially when climbing stairs, squatting, running or sitting for long periods with bent knees. It is common in young, active people.
pelvic-floor-exercises: The pelvic floor is a sling of muscles supporting the bladder, bowel and womb. Strengthening it can reduce urine leakage, improve bladder and bowel control, and support recovery after childbirth or surgery.
pelvic-floor-exercises-and-vaginal-pessa: When pelvic organs such as the bladder, womb or bowel sag into the vagina, this is called prolapse. Pelvic floor exercises can reduce symptoms and may prevent it from worsening, and a vaginal pessary can support the organs without surgery.
pelvic-organ-prolapse: Pelvic organ prolapse happens when the bladder, womb or bowel bulge down into the vagina because the supporting muscles and tissues have weakened. It is common, especially after childbirth and menopause.
peptic-ulcers: A peptic ulcer is an open sore in the lining of the stomach or the first part of the small intestine. It often causes burning upper abdominal pain.
period-pain: Period pain, or dysmenorrhoea, is cramping pain in the lower abdomen before or during menstruation. It is very common, especially in teenagers and young women.
peritoneal-dialysis-for-chronic-kidney-d: Peritoneal dialysis is a form of kidney replacement treatment performed at home. A cleansing fluid is run into the abdomen through a soft tube, where the lining of the abdominal cavity filters waste and excess fluid from the blood.
personalized-medicine: Personalised medicine aims to tailor prevention and treatment to the characteristics of an individual patient, such as genes, the features of a tumour or other biological markers.
phimosis: Phimosis means the foreskin cannot be pulled back over the tip of the penis. In small boys this is normal and usually resolves by itself as they grow.
physical-therapy: Physiotherapy uses movement, exercise, manual techniques and education to restore and maintain physical function. It is used after injury or surgery and for long-term conditions affecting muscles, joints, nerves, the heart and lungs.
pneumonia: Pneumonia is an infection of the lung tissue, usually caused by bacteria or viruses, in which the air sacs fill with fluid or pus. It causes cough, fever and shortness of breath.
podiatry-specialist-foot-care: Podiatrists are specialists in foot care. They treat nails, corns, calluses and foot problems, and help people with diabetes or circulation problems prevent serious foot complications.
post-traumatic-stress-disorder-ptsd: Post-traumatic stress disorder can develop after experiencing or witnessing a terrifying event such as violence, an accident, war, disaster or abuse. People relive the event, avoid reminders and feel constantly on edge.
potty-training: Potty training is the process of helping a child learn to use the toilet. Children are ready at different ages, usually between about two and four years.
pregnancy: Pregnancy lasts about forty weeks and brings many physical and emotional changes. Regular antenatal care, healthy habits and knowing the warning signs help most people have a safe pregnancy and birth.
premature-ejaculation: Premature ejaculation means ejaculating sooner than the man or his partner would like, with little sense of control. It is one of the most common sexual concerns in men and can cause distress and relationship strain.
premenstrual-syndrome: Premenstrual syndrome is a pattern of physical and emotional symptoms that appear in the days before a period and ease once bleeding starts.
prenatal-care-and-maternity-records-in-g: In Germany, antenatal care is provided by midwives and gynaecologists, and the costs of standard check-ups are covered by statutory health insurance.
prenatal-testing: Prenatal tests examine the health and development of an unborn baby. They include routine ultrasound scans and optional tests for chromosomal conditions such as Down syndrome.
pressure-ulcers: Pressure ulcers are injuries to skin and underlying tissue caused by prolonged pressure, usually over bony areas such as the heels, hips, tailbone and elbows.
prevention-diagnosis-treatment-what-is-t: Evidence-based medicine uses the best available research to judge whether health measures work and whether their benefits outweigh harm. It looks at the whole range of medical care: preventing illness, detecting it and treating it.
psa-tests-for-prostate-cancer-screening: The PSA test measures prostate-specific antigen, a protein made by the prostate, in a blood sample. A high level may indicate prostate cancer, but also benign conditions.
psoriasis: Psoriasis is a long-term inflammatory skin condition in which skin cells multiply too fast, producing red, scaly, sometimes itchy patches. It is not contagious.
psoriatic-arthritis-psoriasis-with-joint: Psoriatic arthritis is an inflammatory joint disease that affects some people with psoriasis. It causes pain, swelling and stiffness in joints and tendons, and may damage the joints if untreated.
psychotherapy-providers-in-germany: Several professions offer psychotherapy in Germany, and knowing the differences helps you find suitable help. Statutory health insurance pays for treatment by licensed providers using approved methods.
pubic-lice: Pubic lice are tiny insects that live in coarse body hair, mostly in the genital area, and cause itching. They are usually passed on through close body contact, including sex.
pulmonary-embolism: A pulmonary embolism is a blockage in one of the arteries of the lung, most often caused by a blood clot that has travelled from the deep veins of the legs. It can cause sudden breathlessness and chest pain and may be life-threatening.
quality-assurance-involvement-of-experts: Reliable health information depends on more than good writing. It needs careful checking by experts and input from the people it is meant to help.
retinal-detachment: The retina is the light-sensitive layer at the back of the eye. In retinal detachment it peels away from its supporting tissue, which can cause permanent vision loss if not treated promptly.
rheumatoid-arthritis: Rheumatoid arthritis is a chronic autoimmune disease in which the immune system attacks the lining of the joints, causing pain, swelling and stiffness, often in both hands and feet. Without treatment it can damage joints permanently.
rosacea: Rosacea is a common long-term skin condition causing facial redness, visible small blood vessels, and sometimes bumps and pimples. It mostly affects adults with fair skin and tends to flare and settle.
rubella-german-measles: Rubella is a viral infection that usually causes a mild illness with a rash, but it can seriously harm an unborn baby if a woman is infected during early pregnancy.
scabies: Scabies is a skin infestation caused by tiny mites that burrow into the skin and cause intense itching, especially at night. It spreads through prolonged skin contact and is not a sign of poor hygiene.
scarlet-fever: Scarlet fever is a bacterial infection that accompanies a streptococcal throat infection and causes a typical rash. It is mostly seen in children aged five to fifteen.
schizophrenia: Schizophrenia is a serious mental illness that affects thinking, perception, emotions and behaviour. People may experience hallucinations or delusions and may withdraw from others.
scoliosis-in-teenagers: Scoliosis is a sideways curvature of the spine. The most common type, adolescent idiopathic scoliosis, appears during the growth spurt of puberty without a known cause.
screening: Screening means testing people who have no symptoms in order to find a disease early. It can save lives in some conditions, but not every screening test is worthwhile.
seborrheic-dermatitis: Seborrheic dermatitis is a common, harmless skin condition causing red, flaky, greasy-looking patches, especially on the scalp, face and chest. Dandruff is a mild form.
sensitivity-and-specificity: No medical test is perfect. Sensitivity and specificity describe how well a test finds people with a disease and how well it correctly clears people without it.
shingles: Shingles is a painful rash caused by reactivation of the chickenpox virus, which remains dormant in nerve cells after a person has had chickenpox. It usually appears as a band of blisters on one side of the body and heals in a few weeks.
shoulder-pain: Shoulder pain is common and has many causes, most often problems with the tendons and muscles of the rotator cuff. Most cases improve with time, activity adjustment and exercise.
sinusitis: Acute sinusitis is inflammation of the lining of the sinuses, the air-filled spaces around the nose and eyes, usually following a cold. It causes a blocked nose, facial pressure and sometimes thick discharge.
skin-care-for-eczema: Atopic eczema makes the skin dry, itchy and prone to inflammation. Daily skin care with moisturisers is the foundation of treatment, reducing flare-ups and the need for medicated creams.
sleep-disorders-and-problems-insomnia: Almost everyone has trouble sleeping at some point. Insomnia means persistent difficulty falling asleep, staying asleep or waking too early, together with tiredness or poor functioning during the day.
slipped-disc: A slipped disc occurs when some of the soft centre of a spinal disc pushes through its tougher outer layer and may press on a nearby nerve. It can cause back pain, and when a nerve is affected, pain, numbness or weakness in a leg or arm.
small-objects-in-the-eye: Dust, sand, eyelashes or tiny metal particles often get into the eye and cause scratching, tearing and redness. Most can be washed out safely.
smoking: Smoking is the leading preventable cause of illness and early death, harming nearly every organ. Quitting at any age brings benefits, and the chances of success rise with support and medicine.
speech-and-language-development-disorder: Children learn to speak at different speeds, but some have lasting difficulties understanding or using language or producing speech sounds. Early help improves communication, learning and confidence.
spinal-stenosis-in-the-lower-back-lumbar: Lumbar spinal stenosis is a narrowing of the spinal canal in the lower back that puts pressure on nerves.
spondylolisthesis: Spondylolisthesis occurs when one vertebra slips forward over the one beneath it, most often in the lower back. It may cause back pain, leg pain or no symptoms at all.
standard-check-ups-for-children-and-teen: In Germany, children and teenagers are offered a series of preventive check-ups at set ages, paid for by health insurance. They monitor growth and development, detect problems early, and offer parents the chance to ask questions.
stem-cell-transplantation-for-treating-c: Stem cell transplantation replaces diseased or damaged blood-forming cells with healthy ones. It is used mainly for blood cancers such as leukaemia, lymphoma and myeloma.
steroids-and-other-topical-medications: Anti-inflammatory creams are the main medicine for treating flare-ups of atopic eczema. Topical corticosteroids work well, and when used correctly their risks are small.
stroke: A stroke occurs when blood flow to part of the brain is blocked or a blood vessel bursts. Brain cells are damaged within minutes, so it is a medical emergency.
structure-of-the-feet: The feet carry your whole body weight, absorb shock and propel you forward with every step. Each foot has 26 bones, many joints, strong ligaments, tendons and muscles that work together.
structure-of-the-nails: Nails protect the tips of fingers and toes and help with fine movements such as picking up small objects. Each nail is made of hardened keratin, the same protein found in hair, and grows continuously.
styes-and-chalazia-inflammation-of-the-e: A stye is a painful red lump at the edge of the eyelid caused by infection of an eyelash follicle or gland. A chalazion is a firmer, usually painless lump caused by a blocked oil gland deeper in the lid.
sudden-hearing-loss: Sudden sensorineural hearing loss is a rapid loss of hearing in one ear, usually developing over hours to a few days, without clear cause. It may be accompanied by tinnitus or a feeling of fullness.
sudep-sudden-unexpected-death-in-epileps: SUDEP is the sudden, unexpected death of a person with epilepsy who was otherwise well, not caused by an accident, drowning or a known cause. It is rare but is the leading cause of epilepsy-related death.
support-group-associations-that-help-us-: Patient support groups and associations bring people with the same condition together and give them a voice. They offer practical advice, emotional support and experience-based knowledge.
surgery: An operation can treat disease, repair injury, relieve symptoms or help diagnose a condition. Knowing what happens before, during and after surgery helps you prepare, ask the right questions and take an active part in decisions.
symptoms-after-thrombosis-post-thromboti: Post-thrombotic syndrome is a long-term complication of deep vein thrombosis, a blood clot in the leg veins. The clot can damage vein valves and cause lasting pain, swelling and skin changes in the affected leg.
syphilis: Syphilis is a sexually transmitted infection caused by bacteria, which can be cured with antibiotics, especially if found early. If untreated it can progress over years and damage the heart, brain and other organs.
systematic-searches: To judge whether a treatment works, it is not enough to look at one study or at the studies that happen to be easy to find. A systematic search looks for all relevant research in a planned, repeatable way.
tendon-overuse-injuries-tendinopathy: Tendinopathy is a painful, long-lasting condition of a tendon, usually caused by repeated strain beyond what the tendon can tolerate. It commonly affects the Achilles tendon, shoulder, elbow, knee and hip.
tennis-elbow-and-golfers-elbow: Tennis elbow causes pain on the outside of the elbow and golfer's elbow causes pain on the inside. Both are overuse problems of the tendons that attach forearm muscles to the elbow, and you do not need to play either sport to get them.
tenosynovitis: Tenosynovitis is inflammation of the protective sheath that surrounds a tendon, most commonly in the wrist, hand and fingers. It causes pain, swelling and sometimes difficulty moving, and may follow overuse, injury or infection.
tension-headache: Tension-type headache is the most common type of headache, causing a dull, pressing pain on both sides of the head, often described as a tight band. It is usually mild to moderate and does not stop daily activities.
the-basic-principles-of-evidence-based-m: Evidence-based medicine means making healthcare decisions using the best available research together with clinical experience and the patient's values. It aims to replace guesswork and habit with reliable knowledge about what helps and what harms.
the-breast-cancer-screening-program-in-g: Germany offers women in a defined age range an invitation to mammography screening at regular intervals. The programme aims to find breast cancer early, but like all screening it has benefits and harms.
the-classic-and-asian-forms-of-massage: Massage is a hands-on treatment in which a therapist presses, rubs and moves the soft tissues of the body. People use it for relaxation, muscle tension and pain.
the-first-step-gathering-information: Making good decisions about health starts with finding reliable information. The internet offers an enormous amount of it, but quality varies widely.
the-german-healthcare-system: Germany has a health system with compulsory health insurance, a wide choice of doctors and hospitals and a dense network of services. Understanding how it is organised helps patients, including newcomers, find care and know their rights.
the-history-of-evidence-based-medicine: Evidence-based medicine grew from the idea that treatments should be judged by careful testing, not by tradition or authority alone. Its roots go back centuries, but it became a defined approach in the late twentieth century.
the-innate-and-adaptive-immune-systems: Your immune system protects you against bacteria, viruses, fungi and other invaders, and helps repair damage.
