the-lymphatic-system: The lymphatic system is a network of vessels, nodes and organs that drains fluid from tissues, supports the immune system and helps absorb fats from the gut. When it is working well, you hardly notice it.
the-second-step-evaluating-the-informati: Finding information is only half the task. The second step is to judge whether it is reliable, relevant and applicable to you.
tick-bites: Ticks are small arachnids that feed on blood and can transmit infections such as Lyme disease and tick-borne encephalitis. Most bites cause no harm.
tick-borne-encephalitis-tbe: Tick-borne encephalitis is a viral infection spread by tick bites in parts of Europe and Asia. Many infections cause few or mild symptoms, but some lead to inflammation of the brain and its membranes.
tinea-versicolor: Tinea versicolor is a common, harmless fungal skin condition that causes patches of lighter or darker skin, mainly on the trunk and upper arms. It is not contagious and is caused by yeast that normally lives on skin.
tinnitus: Tinnitus is the perception of sounds such as ringing, buzzing or hissing without an external source. Many people notice it briefly, and for some it becomes persistent and bothersome.
tips-for-adults-with-hearing-loss-or-dea: Hearing loss can make conversation, work and social life more tiring, but practical strategies help. Small changes in the way you and others communicate, together with technology and support services, make daily life easier.
tonsillitis: Tonsillitis is inflammation of the tonsils, the two lumps of tissue at the back of the throat. It causes a sore throat, pain on swallowing and often fever.
tooth-decay: Tooth decay, or caries, is damage to the hard tissue of a tooth caused by acids made by bacteria in dental plaque. It is one of the most common health problems worldwide, yet largely preventable.
torn-acl-anterior-cruciate-ligament-in-t: The anterior cruciate ligament is a strong band inside the knee that keeps the shin bone from sliding forward and stabilises rotation.
torn-meniscus-and-meniscus-damage: The menisci are two C-shaped cartilage pads in each knee that cushion the joint and help stabilise it. A tear can happen suddenly during sport or gradually with age.
travelers-diarrhea: Traveller's diarrhoea affects many people who visit regions with different hygiene standards, usually through contaminated food or water. It causes loose stools, cramps and sometimes nausea, and is usually mild and over within a few days.
trichomoniasis: Trichomoniasis is a common sexually transmitted infection caused by a tiny parasite. Many people have no symptoms, but it can cause vaginal discharge, itching and discomfort.
type-1-diabetes: Type 1 diabetes is a lifelong condition in which the immune system destroys the insulin-producing cells of the pancreas, so the body can no longer make insulin. People need insulin every day to survive.
type-2-diabetes: In type 2 diabetes the body does not respond properly to insulin and eventually cannot make enough. Blood sugar rises, which over years can damage blood vessels and nerves.
types-of-insulin: Insulin comes in several forms that differ in how quickly they start working and how long they last. People with diabetes who need insulin usually combine types to cover meals and to provide a steady background level.
ultrasound-scans-in-pregnancy: Ultrasound uses sound waves to create images of the baby in the womb. It is a safe, painless way to check the baby's growth and development and to date the pregnancy.
underactive-thyroid-hypothyroidism: In hypothyroidism, the thyroid gland produces too little thyroid hormone, slowing the body's metabolism. It causes tiredness, weight gain and feeling cold, and develops slowly.
understanding-chronic-pain: Chronic pain is pain that lasts for more than three months, beyond the usual time of healing. It can arise from an injury or illness, or without a clear cause, and it affects mood, sleep, work and relationships.
understanding-tests-used-to-detect-bone-: Bone problems such as osteoporosis, fractures, infections, tumours and metabolic bone disease are investigated with several tests. Each shows something different, from bone density to the structure of the bone or the activity of bone cells.
understanding-thyroid-tests: Thyroid tests help diagnose an overactive or underactive thyroid, thyroid enlargement and thyroid cancer. They include blood tests, ultrasound and sometimes scans or biopsies.
understanding-urine-tests: Urine tests are simple, painless and provide a lot of information about the kidneys, urinary tract and general health. They can detect infection, kidney problems, diabetes and pregnancy.
unexplained-chronic-cough: A cough that lasts more than eight weeks is called chronic. Common causes include smoking, asthma, reflux, postnasal drip and certain medicines, but sometimes no cause can be found despite tests.
up-to-date-medical-knowledge: Medical knowledge changes continuously. To keep health information reliable, producers must follow research, judge its quality and update their texts.
using-eye-drops-properly: Eye drops are used for many conditions such as glaucoma, infection, allergy and dry eyes. They only work well if they land in the eye and are used at the right times.
using-medication: Medicines can help a great deal, but they can also cause harm if used incorrectly. Taking the right medicine at the right dose and time, and knowing what to watch for, makes treatment safer and more effective.
using-steroids-correctly-and-avoiding-si: Corticosteroids, often called steroids or cortisone, are powerful anti-inflammatory medicines used for asthma, allergies, arthritis, skin conditions and many other illnesses.
uterine-fibroids: Fibroids are non-cancerous growths in the muscle wall of the womb. They are very common, and many women never know they have them.
vaginal-yeast-infection-thrush: Vaginal thrush is a common infection caused by an overgrowth of Candida yeast, which normally lives in small numbers in the vagina. It causes itching, soreness and a thick white discharge.
varicoceles: A varicocele is a swelling of the veins within the scrotum, similar to varicose veins in the legs. It is common, usually on the left side, and often causes no problems.
varicose-veins: Varicose veins are swollen, twisted veins that are visible under the skin, mostly in the legs. Spider veins are tiny red or blue vessels at the surface.
vascular-dementia: Vascular dementia is a form of dementia caused by reduced blood flow to the brain, often after strokes or damage to small vessels. It affects thinking, planning and mood, and can progress in steps or gradually.
ventricular-tachycardia: Ventricular tachycardia is a fast, abnormal heart rhythm that begins in the lower chambers, the ventricles. It can make the heart pump poorly and may degenerate into ventricular fibrillation, which causes sudden cardiac arrest.
vitamin-d-deficiency: Vitamin D deficiency means that the body has too little vitamin D, which is needed for strong bones and muscles. It is common, particularly in winter in northern countries, in people who cover their skin or rarely go outside and in older people.
vocal-nodules: Vocal nodules are small, benign calluses on the vocal cords caused by repeated strain, common in singers, teachers and others who use their voice a lot. They cause hoarseness, a breathy or tired voice and vocal fatigue.
warts: Warts are harmless skin growths caused by human papillomavirus infection of the skin. They are common in children and teenagers and usually disappear by themselves, but may take months or years.
what-are-anticoagulants: Anticoagulants, often called blood thinners, are medicines that make blood clot less easily. They prevent harmful clots that can cause strokes, heart attacks and lung clots, and treat existing clots.
what-are-blood-clots-and-what-causes-the: A blood clot is a clump of blood that has turned from liquid to a semi-solid state. Clotting is a vital protective process that stops bleeding after injury.
what-are-calories: A calorie is a unit of energy. In nutrition, the energy in food is measured in kilocalories, often shortened to calories, or in kilojoules.
what-are-clinical-practice-guidelines: Clinical practice guidelines are documents that summarise the best available evidence and give recommendations on how to prevent, diagnose and treat health conditions.
what-are-dietary-supplements: Dietary supplements are products such as vitamins, minerals, herbal extracts and other substances taken to add to the diet. They are sold in tablets, capsules, powders and drinks.
what-are-digital-health-applications-dig: In Germany, certain apps and web programmes can be prescribed by doctors and psychotherapists like medicines, and the costs are covered by statutory health insurance. They are called digital health applications, or DiGA.
what-are-disease-management-programs-dmp: Disease management programmes in Germany are structured treatment programmes for people with certain long-term illnesses, such as type 2 diabetes, asthma, COPD, coronary heart disease and breast cancer.
what-are-hormones-and-what-do-they-do: Hormones are chemical messengers made by glands and released into the blood. They travel to target organs and tissues and control processes such as growth, metabolism, reproduction, mood and the body's response to stress.
what-are-immunological-tests: Immunological tests examine components of the immune system, such as antibodies, immune cells and signalling molecules.
what-are-ligaments: Ligaments are strong bands of fibrous tissue that connect bones to other bones and stabilise joints. They guide movement and prevent joints from moving too far.
what-are-microbes: Microbes, or microorganisms, are living things too small to see without a microscope. They include bacteria, viruses, fungi and some parasites.
what-are-systematic-reviews-and-meta-ana: A systematic review brings together all the research on a specific question using a planned, transparent method.
what-are-tendons-and-tendon-sheaths: Tendons are strong cords of fibrous tissue that connect muscles to bones and transmit the force that moves the body. Many tendons are surrounded by tendon sheaths, which allow them to glide smoothly.
what-are-the-advantages-and-disadvantage: Professional teeth cleaning removes plaque and tartar that brushing cannot reach, and is often offered as part of dental care. It can leave teeth feeling smooth and fresh.
what-are-the-organs-of-the-immune-system: The immune system is made up of organs, tissues and cells that protect the body from germs and abnormal cells. Some organs produce and train immune cells, while others filter body fluids and collect germs.
what-are-the-treatment-options-for-phimo: Phimosis is a tight foreskin that cannot be pulled back over the head of the penis. When it causes problems, treatment options range from steroid cream to surgery.
what-can-be-done-if-a-baby-is-likely-to-: A baby born before thirty-seven weeks of pregnancy is considered premature. When there are signs of early labour, doctors can sometimes delay birth for a short time and give treatments that improve the baby's chance of doing well.
what-can-help-adults-with-hearing-loss-o: Hearing loss in adults is common and usually gradual. Many options exist, from hearing aids to implants, communication training and assistive technology.
what-can-help-children-with-hearing-loss: Hearing is essential for learning to speak and for development, so early detection and support for children with hearing loss matter greatly.
what-can-help-relieve-anxiety-before-sur: Feeling nervous before an operation is very common. Anxiety can concern the anaesthetic, pain, the result or being away from home.
what-can-you-do-if-you-have-bppv: Benign paroxysmal positional vertigo, or BPPV, causes brief spinning dizziness when you move your head in certain ways, such as turning over in bed or looking up.
what-do-ear-examinations-involve: Ear examinations help doctors find the cause of ear pain, hearing loss, dizziness or ringing in the ears. They are usually painless and quick.
what-do-glucose-tolerance-tests-involve: An oral glucose tolerance test measures how well the body clears sugar from the blood. It is used to diagnose diabetes and prediabetes, and in pregnancy to detect gestational diabetes.
what-do-the-male-sex-organs-do: The male sex organs produce sperm and sex hormones and deliver sperm during sex. They include the testicles, a system of ducts, glands and the penis.
what-does-blood-do: Blood is the body's transport and defence system. It carries oxygen, nutrients, hormones and waste, helps control temperature and fights infection.
what-does-genetic-testing-involve: Genetic tests look at genes, chromosomes or proteins to find changes linked to inherited conditions or to the risk of disease. They are done on a blood or saliva sample.
what-does-your-body-mass-index-say-about: Body mass index, or BMI, is a number calculated from weight and height. It is a quick screening tool for weight categories, but it does not measure body fat directly or say everything about health.
what-happens-during-a-biopsy: A biopsy is a procedure in which a small sample of tissue is taken from the body and examined under a microscope. It is used to diagnose conditions such as cancer, inflammation and infections.
what-happens-during-a-brain-hemorrhage-b: A brain haemorrhage is bleeding inside or around the brain. It is a medical emergency that can cause sudden severe symptoms and lasting damage.
what-happens-during-a-gastroscopy: A gastroscopy is an examination in which a thin flexible tube with a camera is passed through the mouth to look at the gullet, stomach and first part of the small intestine.
what-happens-during-a-lumbar-puncture-sp: A lumbar puncture, or spinal tap, is a procedure in which a thin needle is inserted into the lower back to collect cerebrospinal fluid, the liquid around the brain and spinal cord.
what-happens-during-a-neurological-exami: A neurological examination checks how the brain, spinal cord and nerves are working. It involves simple, painless tests of thinking, senses, movement, reflexes and coordination.
what-happens-during-a-pet-scan: Positron emission tomography, or PET, is an imaging test that shows how tissues work, not only how they look. A small amount of radioactive tracer is injected, and a scanner detects where it collects.
what-happens-during-a-skin-examination: A skin examination is a check of the skin for changes such as unusual moles, spots or rashes. It is used to detect skin cancer early and to diagnose skin conditions.
what-happens-during-an-electroencephalog: An electroencephalogram, or EEG, records the electrical activity of the brain through small sensors placed on the scalp. It is painless and safe.
what-happens-during-cardiac-catheterizat: Cardiac catheterisation is a procedure in which a thin flexible tube, called a catheter, is passed through a blood vessel to the heart.
what-happens-if-you-get-pneumonia-in-the: Hospital-acquired pneumonia is a lung infection that starts at least two days after admission. It can be more serious than pneumonia caught at home because hospital germs are often resistant to some antibiotics and patients may already be weak.
what-happens-in-a-sleep-study: A sleep study, or polysomnography, records body activity during sleep to find out why someone sleeps badly or feels tired by day. It helps to diagnose conditions such as sleep apnoea, restless legs, narcolepsy and abnormal movements in sleep.
what-happens-in-puberty: Puberty is the time when a child's body changes into an adult body and becomes capable of reproduction. It is driven by hormones and brings physical, emotional and social changes.
what-happens-when-you-age: Ageing brings gradual changes in the body and mind. Some are inevitable, but many people stay healthy and active for a long time, and lifestyle makes a big difference.
what-helps-children-cope-with-anxiety-be: Many children feel afraid before an operation. Fear of the unknown, of pain or of being separated from parents is common.
what-helps-reduce-nausea-in-pregnancy: Nausea and vomiting are very common in early pregnancy and are often called morning sickness, although they can occur at any time of day. They usually start around six weeks and ease by about sixteen to twenty weeks.
what-is-a-living-will: A living will, also called an advance directive or advance decision, is a written statement of the medical treatment you want or do not want if you can no longer make decisions yourself.
what-is-an-echocardiogram: An echocardiogram is an ultrasound scan of the heart. It uses sound waves to produce moving pictures of the heart's chambers, valves and walls and shows how well it pumps.
what-is-an-electrocardiogram-ecg: An electrocardiogram, known as an ECG or EKG, is a quick and painless test that records the electrical activity of the heart. It shows heart rate and rhythm and can help detect heart attack, rhythm disorders and strain on the heart.
what-is-an-inflammation: Inflammation is the body's response to injury, infection or irritation. It is a protective process that helps healing, but when it is excessive or lasts too long it can damage tissue and contribute to many diseases.
what-is-evidence-based-medicine: Evidence-based medicine means making health decisions by combining the best available research, the doctor's clinical experience and the patient's values and circumstances.
what-is-joint-aspiration: Joint aspiration, or arthrocentesis, is a procedure in which a needle is used to withdraw fluid from a joint. It is done to find the cause of joint swelling or pain, to relieve pressure and sometimes to inject medicine.
what-is-laparoscopy: Laparoscopy, also called keyhole surgery, is a way of looking inside the abdomen or pelvis, and performing operations, through small cuts. A thin tube with a camera and light, called a laparoscope, is inserted.
what-is-nitrous-oxide-laughing-gas-and-w: Nitrous oxide, known as laughing gas, is a colourless gas used in medicine and dentistry to reduce pain and anxiety. It is also misused as a recreational drug, which carries real health risks.
what-is-normal-sleep: Sleep is a vital, active state in which the body repairs itself and the brain processes memories. How much sleep people need varies, and so does the timing.
what-is-occupational-therapy: Occupational therapy helps people of all ages to do the everyday activities that matter to them, such as dressing, cooking, working, studying and playing, when illness, injury, disability or ageing makes this difficult.
what-is-overdiagnosis: Overdiagnosis means finding a condition that would never have caused symptoms or harm during a person's life, and then treating it. It happens when tests detect real abnormalities that are not dangerous.
what-is-psychotherapy-and-what-does-it-i: Psychotherapy, or talking therapy, is a treatment for mental health problems and emotional difficulties. A trained therapist works with you through conversation and exercises to understand and change thoughts, feelings and behaviour.
what-is-speech-therapy: Speech and language therapy helps people with difficulties in speaking, understanding, reading, voice, fluency or swallowing. It is provided by trained therapists to children and adults, and aims to improve communication and quality of life.
what-is-the-structure-of-hair-and-how-do: Hair is made of a tough protein called keratin. Each hair grows from a follicle in the skin and goes through cycles of growth, rest and shedding.
what-is-voice-therapy: Voice therapy is a treatment that helps people with voice problems, such as hoarseness, strain, weak voice or loss of voice. A speech and language therapist teaches exercises and healthy habits.
what-kind-of-lung-function-tests-are-the: Lung function tests measure how well the lungs work, including how much air they hold and how quickly air moves in and out. They help diagnose asthma, chronic obstructive pulmonary disease and other lung conditions, and monitor treatment.
what-kinds-of-allergy-tests-are-there: Allergy tests help find out which substances trigger an allergic reaction. They include skin tests, blood tests and supervised challenge tests.
what-kinds-of-eye-examinations-are-there: Eye examinations check vision and the health of the eye. They detect problems such as short or long sight, glaucoma, cataracts, macular degeneration and diabetic eye disease, often before symptoms appear.
what-role-does-breast-density-play: Breast density describes how much of the breast is made up of glandular and connective tissue compared with fat, as seen on a mammogram. Dense breasts are common and normal.
what-screening-tests-does-german-public-: Statutory health insurance in Germany pays for a range of preventive check-ups and screening tests for different ages.
what-types-of-studies-are-there: Medical research uses different kinds of studies to answer different questions. Some test whether a treatment works, while others look at causes of disease or how common it is.
when-are-statins-recommended: Statins are medicines that lower cholesterol and reduce the risk of heart attack and stroke. They are recommended mainly for people who already have heart or vascular disease, and for some people with a high risk.
when-is-a-c-section-an-option: A caesarean section is an operation in which a baby is born through a cut in the mother's abdomen and womb. It may be planned in advance or done in an emergency when vaginal birth is unsafe.
which-vaccinations-are-recommended-in-ge: In Germany, the Standing Committee on Vaccination (STIKO) at the Robert Koch Institute publishes recommendations for children, adults and special groups. They are updated regularly, so check the current schedule with your doctor.
why-are-vitamin-d-supplements-recommende: Vitamin D is needed for strong bones and teeth, as it helps the body absorb calcium.
wisdom-teeth: Wisdom teeth are the third molars at the back of the mouth, usually appearing between ages seventeen and twenty-five. Many people have no problems, while others experience pain, infection or crowding.
worms-in-children-pinworms: Pinworms are small, white, thread-like worms that live in the bowel and are among the most common worm infections in children. They are harmless but cause itching around the anus, particularly at night.
wrist-injuries: The wrist is a complex joint made of many small bones, ligaments and tendons, and it is often injured by falls, sports or repetitive use. Injuries range from sprains to fractures.
